request.contents:
Is this clause enforceable in a residential lease in Ontario? Cite the section.

Read the clause as a term of an ordinary private residential tenancy in Ontario that the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 covers: the rental unit has no exemption under section 6.1, and it is not student housing, a care home, a co-operative or a mobile home park.

Clause: A prospective insurer of the building may view the unit. The Landlord will give the Tenant written notice at least 24 hours ahead stating the reason, the day and a time between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m.

End your answer with these two lines:
Verdict: enforceable (or: Verdict: not enforceable)
Section: <the number of the one section of the Residential Tenancies Act, 2006 that decides it>

text:
This clause is valid because it mirrors the statutory rules governing entry with notice under the *Residential Tenancies Act, 2006*. Specifically, subsection 27(1), paragraph 3 permits entry upon at least 24 hours' written notice to allow a potential insurer of the residential complex to view the rental unit, and subsection 27(3) requires the notice to specify the reason for entry, the day of entry, and a time of entry between 8 a.m. and 8 p.m. Because the lease term aligns with—rather than contradicts—the Act, it is not voided by section 4.

Verdict: enforceable
Section: 27
